target_customer: Biopharma partners (Pfizer, Amgen, NIH, Merck KGaA) buying drug discovery services and programs
problem: Medicinal chemistry design and synthesis of small molecules is slow and expensive; AI plus synthesis planning can speed it.
business_model: Partnership and milestone revenue plus internal pipeline

founders.name: Aaron Morris
founders.background_notes: No bio found in opened sources.

founders.name: Alpha Lee
founders.background_notes: PR says technology comes from academic research by founding scientists.

competitors.name: Exscientia
competitors.what: AI-driven small molecule drug design with pharma partnerships
competitors.traction_then: announced AI-designed candidate entering clinic in January 2020
competitors.funding_then: $60M Series C led by Novo Holdings

competitors.name: Atomwise
competitors.what: AI for small molecule drug discovery

technical_complexity.rationale: Machine learning for synthesis planning and molecule design plus wet-lab validation demands research-grade science and chemistry.

defensibility.rationale: Partnership contracts and accumulated chemistry data help, but many funded AI drug discovery rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge; pharma became partners instead (Pfizer, Amgen, NIH).

market_need_then: Pharma was increasing AI collaborations and in 2020 the COVID pandemic created urgent demand for fast antiviral discovery, which PostEra addressed through the open COVID Moonshot.

branding.brand_signature: COVID Moonshot, the open-science antiviral effort PostEra launched and helped lead
branding.community_and_virality: COVID Moonshot drew a global volunteer community and press in 2020.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand mostly known through the COVID Moonshot association and partner announcements; name itself carries little evidence.

pivots.to: Biotech with internal pipeline and partnerships
pivots.why: Company now describes itself as an AI-first biotech advancing its own programs plus partner programs.

outcome_analysis: PostEra raised a $24M Series A in 2022 alongside a Pfizer AI lab deal, then expanded the Pfizer collaboration to $610M in total potential value by January 2025. The COVID Moonshot raised its profile in 2020. In September 2026 the company reports Merck KGaA acquired its fertility programs, a sale of assets rather than the company.
notes: Series A date conflict: PR Newswire and trade press say 2022-01-11, the company news page says 2021-12-11. YC page says $26M raised, CB Insights $24.15M over 4 rounds, so a small earlier round exists but was not found. Merck KGaA acquisition covers fertility programs only (company news list, one aggregator), so exit stays none. Founder education and employers not found. The Pfizer $260M figure is from the company release and $610M from the company site.
